title: Fed holds its target range at 3.75% to 4%, with two votes for a hike
summary: The Federal Open Market Committee left the federal funds target range at 3-3/4 to 4 percent on October 28; Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase.
body: The Federal Reserve's policy committee kept the federal funds rate target range at 3-3/4 to 4 percent at its October 27-28, 2026 meeting. The vote was 10 to 2.

Governor Lisa D. Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth M. Hammack dissented, preferring to raise the range by a quarter percentage point. The statement said economic activity is expanding at a strong pace and that inflation remains elevated.
The committee's next scheduled decision is in December.
why: The fed funds rate does not set mortgage rates directly, but it drives short-term borrowing costs: HELOCs, construction loans and many hard money and bridge loans price off short-term rates. Two dissents in favor of a hike are a signal to stress test flips and BRRRR projects at higher financing costs with the fix and flip calculator and the BRRRR calculator.
